subject: botany_2
question_text: Explain the role of the pink colour pigment in the root nodule of legume plants. What is it called?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.50, printed question 152. insider_note: The name and the job. Leg-haemoglobin is an oxygen scavenger: it binds oxygen inside the nodule so that nitrogenase is protected. The role is the half most often left out.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What it is called
steps.margin_note: One line. Spell leg-haemoglobin in full.
lines: The pink pigment in the root nodules of legume
steps.why: The name says what it is: a haemoglobin-like pigment, and haemoglobin is a molecule that binds oxygen — which is already the answer to the second half.
common_mistakes: Calling it haemoglobin. It is LEG-haemoglobin, found in legume nodules.
Calling it chlorophyll. Chlorophyll is green; this pigment is pink.
steps.memory_tip: Legume plus haemoglobin: the name carries both the place and the job.

steps.label: Its role
steps.margin_note: Name the enzyme and say why it needs protecting. The guide writes 'dinitrogenase' for the same enzyme complex; NCERT writes nitrogenase.

lines.text: It keeps oxygen away from nitrogenase

lines: Leg-haemoglobin binds oxygen inside the nodule.
This protects the NITROGENASE enzyme, which is
So nitrogen fixation can go on.
steps.why: Nitrogenase is destroyed by oxygen, so nitrogen fixation is only possible if something keeps the oxygen level inside the nodule very low. That is why leg-haemoglobin is called an oxygen scavenger, and the term is worth writing.
common_mistakes: Saying it carries oxygen TO the bacteria. Its job is to keep oxygen AWAY from nitrogenase.
Naming no enzyme. Nitrogenase is what is being protected, and it is the mark.
steps.memory_tip: Pink pigment, oxygen sponge: it mops up what the enzyme cannot survive.
